definitions.explanation: Describes the state of spending more than the planned or allotted budget. A common wasei-eigo compound mixing Japanese and English.

examples.japanese: リフォームが{予算|よさん}オーバーしてしまった。
examples.english: The renovation ended up going over budget.

examples.japanese: {予算|よさん}オーバーにならないように、{毎月|まいつき}の{支出|ししゅつ}をしっかり{管理|かんり}している。
examples.english: I carefully manage my monthly spending so I don't go over budget.

notes:
USAGE:
A Japanese-English hybrid expression using {予算|よさん} (budget) + オーバー (over, from English). Can be used as a noun ({予算|よさん}オーバーだ) or with する ({予算|よさん}オーバーする). Common in everyday conversation about personal finance, shopping, and project management.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {予算|よさん}オーバーする (to go over budget)
- {予算|よさん}オーバーになる (to end up over budget)
- {大幅|おおはば}な{予算|よさん}オーバー (a major budget overrun)

SIMILAR EXPRESSIONS:
- {予算|よさん}を{超|こ}える: to exceed the budget — more formal phrasing
- {予算|よさん}{超過|ちょうか}: budget excess — formal/written
